gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-cypr: Noto Sans Cypro Minoan reads open and spacious, its terminals cut back to leave generous gaps. Red Hat Display sits above it drawing every curve with one marker-like line, so the bold heading feels solid while the sans-serif text stays light.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-hani: Every letter looks bent from a single piece of wire, thick and confident. Noto Sans Hanifi Rohingya takes over below with a visibly gaping c, softening the page into something friendlier than the heading alone.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-hatr: Noto Sans Hatran reads like a plain sans with a wide, funnel-shaped throat in every e, welcoming and easy to move through. Red Hat Display, traced with one marker, gives it a firm headline.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-insc: Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi reads unclogged, with small counters that stay clear and contemporary. Red Hat Display is best at bold, plain, unshaded lines that grab attention; Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi is best at quietly carrying the words that follow.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-java: Red Hat Display holds its curves at full thickness right through every turn, which gives headings a bold, solid look. And Noto Sans Javanese does the quieter job, keeping its counters connected to the space outside so the text stays clean.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-kawi: Red Hat Display gives its crossbars the same heft as its stems, so each bold heading letter looks drawn with one marker. Noto Sans Kawi, a plain sans with open-jawed c shapes, keeps a long page easy.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-line: Noto Sans Linear A reads clean and plain, its c gaping visibly at any size. Red Hat Display is best at outlined, drafting-pen headings with one constant nib width, while Noto Sans Linear A is best at quiet, steady text.

Red Hat Display keeps a flat, unvarying line weight in every letter, giving headings a bold, marker-drawn confidence. But Noto Sans Linear B is the smoother partner, its sans letters sending a clear path around each bend.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-mani: Noto Sans Manichaean reads modern and clean, with open-mouthed e crossbars. Red Hat Display leads above it with round bowls that never swell, so a long passage in the sans flows smoothly beneath.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-mong: Noto Sans Mongolian reads neutral and modern, its terminals flaring outward in a friendly way. And Red Hat Display, bold with no thick or thin strokes, works well if you give it a noticeably larger size.
